comments.body:
Review remediation record (2026-08-21) for this ticket's plan — moved out of the description to fit the plan-review admission cap. What was factually wrong in the original plan and what was corrected:

- FALSE CLAIM: "the completion gate BYPASSES the ref resolver at `close_autoresume.py:141`". It does not. Ref resolution is already uniform: every gate, the completion gate included, resolves through `gate_source.resolve_gate_handle` (`src/rebar/llm/gate_source.py:76`), the completion path reaching it at `src/rebar/llm/completion.py:149` via `close_autoresume.py:235`. Line 141 is `resolve_ref(ref or "HEAD", root, fetch=False)` inside `_reusable_attested_pass` — a cache-hit equality check comparing the close target against the signed `verified-at-sha`, not gate-source selection. Correction recorded as a constraint: routing THAT call through `resolve_gate_handle` would let the reuse check honour `REBAR_GATE_REF` and accept a certified PASS pinned to a DIFFERENT sha than the one being closed. What actually differs between gates is the arguments, not the resolver: the completion gate deliberately pins `source="attested"`, `ref=(ref or "HEAD")`, `fetch=False` (epic `raze-vet-ditch` S4, rationale at `close_autoresume.py:225-234`) so the verdict is reproducible, branch-independent and signable; that pinning is load-bearing and unchanged by this work.

- UNDERCOUNT: the plan said the CI "this change predates the gate script" shell guard appears twelve times. It appears 24 times across `.github/`: `_build-and-test.yml:145,159,181,195,210,288,377,570`; `_optionality.yml:108,114,133`; `_mutation.yml:64` (the 12 in scope); plus `.github/actions/docs-gates/action.yml` x10 and `gerrit-verify.yaml:323,332` (12 out of scope, which keep their inline guards). Bug `sapphire-vulnerable-fruitfly` added one of these guards and `anxious-resistant-urson` was a missing one.

- MECHANISM GAP: the plan assumed a composite action could replace the inline guards directly. It cannot abort a caller's `run:` block — `uses:` cannot appear mid-`run:`, and a composite exiting 0 does not terminate the calling step. The design was changed to a guard step emitting a `present` output, with the existing work gated on `if: steps.<id>.outputs.present == 'true'`. Four sites carry behaviour a bare skip would silently drop and are now called out explicitly: `_mutation.yml:64` (also writes `matrix={"shard":[]}` and `has-shards=false` to `$GITHUB_OUTPUT` on skip, pinned by `tests/unit/test_ci_workflow_parity.py:250-267`); `_optionality.yml:108,114` (two generators guarded independently inside one step per bug `5bc6-5496-4e17-403a`); `_build-and-test.yml:181,195` (inverted `[ -f ]/else` with no `exit 0`, continuing afterwards); `_build-and-test.yml:377` (guards the DATA file `.github/git-version-floor.txt` via `$floorfile` and continues into a `sort -V` that can `exit 1`).

- OVER-MERGE RISK: the plan implied `code_review_enabled` would be folded into `gate_enabled`. Recorded as a divergence that must be preserved — `code_review_enabled` (`src/rebar/llm/workflow/gate_dispatch.py:277`) keeps its name, its `repo_root`-only signature, its broad `except Exception` and its silent `False` (`gate_dispatch.py:283-286`). Routing it through `gate_enabled` would narrow the catch to `ConfigError` (crashing code review instead of degrading it), add a stderr warning on every unreadable-config code review, and demand a `ticket_id` that code review, dispatching against a CHANGE rather than a ticket, has no source for.

- TEST-SEAM HAZARD identified: 20 `monkeypatch.setattr(gate_dispatch, "code_review_enabled", ...)` sites across 6 files and 24 `monkeypatch.setattr(_gates, "gate_enabled", ...)` sites across 20 files bind those two symbols. If callers switch to calling `gate_policy.resolve(...)` directly, every one of those patches becomes inert but still green — the tests keep passing while exercising the real config. An acceptance criterion now pins that both symbols remain what production calls.

- PATH CORRECTION: `test_close_gate_unreadable_config_2091.py` lives under `tests/interfaces/lifecycle/`, not `tests/unit/`; the pinning commands were fixed accordingly.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
Second remediation pass (2026-08-21). The previous pass corrected the plan's false claim that the completion gate bypasses the ref resolver. Verifying the REST of the plan against the tree disproved BOTH consolidations it proposed, so the story has been re-scoped. Evidence:

1. "The four gates each answer enabled?/what ref?/fail mode? separately." FALSE on all three axes.
   - Ref/source: uniform already. Every gate resolves through `gate_source.resolve_gate_handle` (`src/rebar/llm/gate_source.py:76`); completion reaches it at `src/rebar/llm/completion.py:149` via `close_autoresume.py:234`.
   - Enabled: three of the four gates already call ONE function, `gates.gate_enabled` (`src/rebar/_commands/gates.py:91`) — from `gates.py:196` (plan-review close), `gates.py:282` (plan-review claim) and `close_precheck.py:489` (completion close).
   - Fail mode on an unreadable config: uniform already, and the plan described it wrongly. The plan said `gate_enabled` is "tri-state" and "warns to stderr". It is neither: `GateState` (`gates.py:49`) is two-state — the `UNREADABLE` member was REMOVED by operator ruling 39f8-ae7c — and an unreadable config RAISES a chained `ConfigError` (`gates.py:115-120`). The plan's cited line ranges for that behaviour (`gates.py:127-138`, `gates.py:286,292-297`) point at unrelated code: 127-138 is the `gate_ran` predicate docstring and 292 is `description_cap_warning`. The `unavailable` dict the plan attributed to config unreadability is at `gates.py:264-271` and comes from an ATTESTATION-verify failure, not from the config read; a DISABLED close gate returns a `"disabled"` payload (`gates.py:207-212`).
   What actually differs between the three callers is only what each does with a DISABLED answer — `False`, a `"disabled"` payload, `"gate_off"`. That is caller policy, not a duplicated computation, and the fourth reader (`code_review_enabled`, `gate_dispatch.py:277`) must keep its divergent broad-`except`/silent-`False` posture, as the plan itself required. A `GatePolicy` resolver would therefore be pure indirection over an already-shared implementation: no copy removed, no behaviour changed. Dropped.

2. "Replace the twelve in-scope guards with a composite action." MECHANICALLY IMPOSSIBLE, not merely awkward. Any shared owner — composite action, shell helper, Python module — lives in the repo, so it is absent on exactly the pre-gate trees the guard exists to serve. On such a tree the guard would skip gates whose scripts DO exist, or the job would fail resolving a missing local `uses:`. This is pinned locally, not inferred: `tests/unit/test_ci_workflow_parity.py::test_mutation_selector_skips_pre_gate_trees_without_weakening_current_trees` executes the step's `run:` body under bash in an EMPTY directory and asserts exit 0 plus the message on stdout (confirmed passing in this worktree); a body that shells out to a repo file cannot satisfy it. `gerrit-verify.yaml:206` already carries the same exposure for `uses: ./.github/actions/docs-gates` itself.

3. Guard count re-verified: 24 occurrences of "change predates the gate" across `.github/` — `docs-gates/action.yml` x10, `_build-and-test.yml` x8, `_optionality.yml` x3, `gerrit-verify.yaml` x2, `_mutation.yml` x1. The plan's per-site line numbers were checked and are correct (they point at the `if [ -f … ]` line, not the echo).

4. NEW FINDING while auditing: the guard is applied unevenly. `test.yml:174,176` invoke `scripts/check_readme_quickstart.py` and `scripts/probe_rebar.py` with no guard, while `gerrit-verify.yaml:324,333` guard those same two scripts. That is the shape of bug `anxious-resistant-urson` (a gate step with no guard) recurring.

Re-scope: since the construct cannot have a shared implementation, the achievable equivalent of consolidation is ONE OWNER FOR THE INVARIANT — the epic's own durable shape, a test a drifting copy cannot pass. The story now delivers a parity test asserting (a) every gate step in the six affected files carries an `-f` guard for the file it needs or a mandatory-reason `# predates-gate-ok:` marker, and (b) every guarded step body exits 0 with the canonical message when run in an empty directory, generalising the single-site mutation pin to all of them. Workflow edits are comment-only; genuine gaps are filed and linked rather than fixed here, because adding a guard changes which gates run on an old base and is its own reviewable change.

Note for the epic's net-negative-lines criterion: this child adds a test and removes no lines, because the consolidation it was scoped for was proven unavailable. It should be counted with the hardening children, not the consolidation children.

comments.body:
Implementation evidence (2026-08-21).

WHAT LANDED: `tests/unit/test_predates_gate_guard_parity.py` (new, 4 tests) plus comment-only marker additions in four workflow files.

Detection rule (resolving the review's E2 advisory, which correctly noted the plan said "reads a repo data file" without a heuristic): a step "runs a repo-local gate file" when its `run:` body — after `${{ … }}` removal and simple `name=path` shell-assignment substitution — mentions a path under `scripts/`, `tests/`, `docs/` with extension `.py`/`.txt`/`.json`, or under `.github/` with `.txt`/`.json`, AND that path is currently tracked by `git ls-files`. The tracked-file requirement is what draws the boundary the advisory asked for: an ephemeral or generated path is not tracked, so it never counts. The `.github/git-version-floor.txt` case is reached through the assignment substitution (`floorfile=…` then `-f "$floorfile"`).

MUTATION EVIDENCE (each mutation applied, test run, then reverted):
- Changed `exit 0` to `exit 3` in the real mutation-selector guard (`_mutation.yml`) -> `test_empty_tree_every_guarded_step_skips_cleanly` FAILED naming that exact step. Restored -> green.
- Forced `unguarded_paths` to return `[]` -> `test_a_step_that_drops_its_guard_is_caught` FAILED (`assert None is not None`). Restored -> green.
- Deleted the empty-reason rejection branch in `step_violation` -> `test_a_marker_without_a_reason_is_rejected` FAILED. Restored -> green.
- Changed `SKIP_MESSAGE` to "change predates the gates" -> three tests FAILED. Restored -> green.
Before any marker was added, `test_completeness_every_gate_step_is_guarded_or_marked` was RED naming all seven unguarded steps — the RED-for-the-right-reason baseline, not an ImportError.

MARKERS ADDED (7 steps). Five are genuinely guard-free, with the reason recorded inline: `_mutation.yml` "Run mutation shard" (the job's `if: needs.selector.outputs.has-shards == 'true'` is driven by the selector's own guard); `gerrit-verify.yaml` "Normalize the conclusion" and "Summarize the jobs that did not succeed" (the preceding step is a plain `actions/checkout` of the DEFAULT branch, fetched precisely because the script must be trusted — the patchset's base age cannot make it absent); `test.yml` "Publish the verdict…" (the job's `if` restricts it to `schedule`/`workflow_dispatch`). Two are real gaps, filed and linked `discovered_from` this ticket rather than fixed here: `cushy-soldierly-sunbear` (e818-564e-d3b6-4eaa) for `test.yml` golden-path, whose two scripts `gerrit-verify.yaml:324,333` already guards — the epic's exact motivating pattern of a fix landing in one copy while its twin stays broken; and `marauding-hornblende-bluet` (d93e-92ce-e2d0-4033) for `_optionality.yml`'s degradation-path step, which IS on the Verified lane and would exit 4 on a pre-gate tree, the same bug `1909-c1a7-9f20-440f` the step below it already fixed.

AC NOTE — "only comment lines": the workflow diff is comment additions plus three `run:` scalars rewritten as block scalars (`_mutation.yml` "Run mutation shard", `test.yml` "README quickstart golden-path" and "End-to-end CLI probe"), because a YAML comment above a step is not part of the `run:` string the marker has to live in. Shell semantics are unchanged (same single command, same redirection); `tests/unit/test_ci_workflow_parity.py` passes unchanged, and `make lint` (actionlint + zizmor over all workflows) is clean.

GATES: `make lint` clean; `make typecheck` clean (626 files); `python scripts/check_complexity_baseline.py --check` reports `new=0 increased=0 stale=3`.

compiled_state.description:
## Context / Problem
The CI shell guard `[ -f <path> ] || { echo "… (change predates the gate) — skipping"; exit 0; }`
is written **24 times** across `.github/`: `_build-and-test.yml:145,159,181,195,210,288,377,570`;
`_optionality.yml:108,114,133`; `_mutation.yml:64`; `gerrit-verify.yaml:323,332`;
`.github/actions/docs-gates/action.yml` x10. It exists because a patchset whose base predates a
gate script must not fail `Verified` on that gate. Two defects came from copies drifting apart:
`anxious-resistant-urson` (a gate step with NO guard) and `sapphire-vulnerable-fruitfly` (a guard
added late). The guard is also applied unevenly today — `test.yml:174,176` invoke
`scripts/check_readme_quickstart.py` and `scripts/probe_rebar.py` with no guard at all, while
`gerrit-verify.yaml:324,333` guard the same two scripts.

## Finding 1 — the CI guard CANNOT move into a shared repo file
A shared owner (composite action, shell helper, Python module) lives in the repo, so it is absent
on exactly the pre-gate trees the guard serves; the guard would then skip gates whose scripts DO
exist, or the job would fail resolving a missing local `uses:`. This is not a judgement call: the
existing pin `tests/unit/test_ci_workflow_parity.py::test_mutation_selector_skips_pre_gate_trees_without_weakening_current_trees`
executes the step's `run:` body under `bash` in an **empty directory** and requires exit 0 plus the
message on stdout — a body that shells out to a repo file cannot satisfy that. `gerrit-verify.yaml:206`
already carries the same exposure for `uses: ./.github/actions/docs-gates` itself.

## Finding 2 — the four gates ALREADY share one resolver
- Ref/source resolution is uniform: every gate, completion included, goes through
  `gate_source.resolve_gate_handle` (`src/rebar/llm/gate_source.py:76`), completion reaching it at
  `src/rebar/llm/completion.py:149` via `close_autoresume.py:234`.
- Flag resolution for three of the four gates is one function, `gates.gate_enabled`
  (`src/rebar/_commands/gates.py:91`), called from `gates.py:196` (plan-review close),
  `gates.py:282` (plan-review claim) and `close_precheck.py:489` (completion close).
- Its unreadable-config posture is already uniform and is **not** a warn-and-continue: it raises a
  chained `ConfigError` (`gates.py:115-120`), and `GateState` (`gates.py:49`) is two-state — the
  `UNREADABLE` member was REMOVED by operator ruling 39f8-ae7c. What differs between the three is
  only what each CALLER does with a `DISABLED` answer (`False` / a `"disabled"` payload /
  `"gate_off"`), which is caller policy, not a duplicated computation.
- The one separate reader, `code_review_enabled` (`llm/workflow/gate_dispatch.py:277`), must keep
  its divergence: its broad `except Exception` → silent `False` (`gate_dispatch.py:283-286`) is
  what degrades code review to inert; `gate_enabled` would instead raise, would warn, and would
  demand a `ticket_id` that code review — dispatching against a CHANGE — has no source for.

So the resolver named in this story's original plan would be pure indirection over an existing
shared implementation, with no behaviour change and no copy removed. It is dropped.

## Approach
Deliver the achievable equivalent of consolidation for a construct that cannot be shared: **one
owner for the invariant**, in the epic's guard shape — a test a drifting copy cannot pass.
Add `tests/unit/test_predates_gate_guard_parity.py`:

1. **Completeness.** For every `run:` step in the six files above that invokes a repo-relative
   `scripts/*.py` or reads a repo data file, assert the step body contains an `-f` test for that
   exact path together with the canonical `change predates the gate` message. A step that
   legitimately needs no guard carries `# predates-gate-ok: <reason>`; an empty or missing reason
   fails the test.
2. **Behaviour.** For every guarded step, execute its `run:` body (with `${{ … }}` expressions
   substituted to empty strings) under `bash --noprofile --norc -eo pipefail` in an EMPTY
   directory with `GITHUB_OUTPUT` set, and assert exit 0 and the canonical message on stdout —
   generalising the single-site mutation pin above to all of them.

Guard form follows the parent epic `airborne-wellloved-kingfisher`: match the conjunction
(`-f <path>` together with the canonical message), never one common token; mandatory-reason escape
marker; behaviour pinned only by the existing named tests.

## Constraint: four sites carry behaviour a bare skip would drop
`_mutation.yml:64` also writes `matrix={"shard":[]}` and `has-shards=false` to `$GITHUB_OUTPUT`;
`_optionality.yml:108,114` guard two generators **independently inside one step** per bug
`5bc6-5496-4e17-403a`; `_build-and-test.yml:181,195` use the inverted `[ -f ]/else` form with no
`exit 0`; `_build-and-test.yml:377` guards the DATA file `.github/git-version-floor.txt` and
continues into a `sort -V` that can `exit 1`. The test asserts the guard, never the step's shape,
so all four keep their current bodies.

## Constraint: no workflow behaviour changes in this story
This story adds no guard and removes none — adding a guard changes which gates run on an old
base, which is its own reviewable change. Every step the completeness check surfaces gets a
`# predates-gate-ok:` marker instead: for a step that needs no guard the reason says why, and for
a step that is a genuine gap the reason cites a ticket filed and linked `discovered_from` this
one. Workflow edits in this story are therefore comment-only.

## Scope
`tests/unit/test_predates_gate_guard_parity.py` (new); `.github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml`,
`_optionality.yml`, `_mutation.yml`, `gerrit-verify.yaml`, `test.yml`,
`.github/actions/docs-gates/action.yml` (comment-only `# predates-gate-ok:` markers, if needed).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Every gate step in the six files either carries an `-f` guard naming the file it needs, or a
      `# predates-gate-ok:` marker with a non-empty reason; checked by
      `pytest tests/unit/test_predates_gate_guard_parity.py -k completeness`.
- [ ] Every guarded step body exits 0 and prints `change predates the gate` when run in an empty
      directory; checked by `pytest tests/unit/test_predates_gate_guard_parity.py -k empty_tree`.
- [ ] An escape marker whose reason is empty is rejected; checked by a negative case in that file
      feeding a synthetic step with a bare `# predates-gate-ok:` and asserting the check fails.
- [ ] A step that drops its guard is caught; checked by a negative case feeding a synthetic
      guard-free step and asserting the completeness check fails.
- [ ] No existing CI behaviour changes; checked by `git diff origin/main -- .github/` showing only
      comment lines, and by `pytest tests/unit/test_ci_workflow_parity.py` passing unchanged.
- [ ] Every marker whose reason cites a gap names a ticket linked `discovered_from` this one;
      checked by `rebar show 7e0d-7815-4425-4fdb` listing one link per such marker.
